newsitem.title: UK: British pop stars Oasis to record new album.
newsitem.headline: British pop stars Oasis to record new album.

text.p: British pop superstars Oasis, rocked by rumours of a split, told anxious fans on Tuesday they would release a new album next year.
After abruptly pulling out of a concert tour of the United States last week, the million-selling band said it would start work on their long-awaited third album next month.

When their tour collapsed amid reports that singer Liam Gallagher and his guitarist brother Noel had come to blows, their record company denied reports Oasis would split but confirmed they would not be touring for the foreseeable future.
The Oasis story caused a furore in the British media, obsessed with the most popular British band since the Beatles split up in 1970.
Liam once boasted: "We are bigger than Jesus. We will be as big as the Beatles, if not bigger."
In their latest statement, Oasis denied reports of internal differences, disappointing ticket sales in the U.S. and suggestions that Liam's girlfriend was breaking up the band.

"The reason for the premature return of the band has nothing to do with recent UK tabloid hysteria (eg poor ticket sales, Liam's fiancee Patsy Kensit, sibling rivalry or internal differences)," the statement said.
"It was a decision taken solely by Noel Gallagher on behalf of his four friends. We look forward to presenting our fans with a new album in the summer of '97."

Oasis, whose first two albums have sold 20 million copies, have led a "Britpop" revival. A summer concert drew a record crowd of 250,000, but the feuding between the Gallagher brothers has generated as many headlines as the music.
Oasis's record company Creation is 49 percent owned by Sony Music.
